extracted.intended_audience: travelers and general readers (especially U.S. citizens) seeking country facts, culture, and travel/safety guidance about Australia
extracted.subtask_description: A country profile summarizing Australia's culture, geography, economy, demographics, and practical travel information (visiting rules, safety, driving, medical, and legal issues) aimed at prospective visitors and students of the country.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultural attribute — sense of humor
rubrics_metrics.description: Australians have a good sense of humor and anything is a topic for humor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page presents this as a general cultural trait; useful as etiquette context for visitors or for writers/performers aiming to connect with Australian audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common local expressions / greeting etiquette
rubrics_metrics.description: Australian catchphrases include “G'day mate!”, “no worries”, “not a problem” and “Good on yer!”.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Knowing and using common informal phrases can help social interactions; the page also mentions visiting without a prior appointment (fragmentary) as a social practice to be aware of.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crime awareness and personal security precautions
rubrics_metrics.description: Robberies, burglaries, assault, and auto theft are common in larger cities; weapons are increasingly used in such crimes; foreign visitors in popular tourist areas are targets for pickpockets, purse-snatchers, and petty thieves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take appropriate security precautions, especially at night; be careful consuming alcohol with unfamiliar people because drink spiking can occur; maintain vigilance and avoid becoming a target of opportunity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not purchase counterfeit or pirated goods
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not buy counterfeit and pirated goods, even if they are widely available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not only are bootlegs illegal in the United States, but purchasing them may also violate local law; you can be prosecuted under U.S. law for buying pirated goods abroad.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obey local laws — your passport doesn't protect you
rubrics_metrics.description: While traveling in Australia, you are subject to its laws even if you are a U.S. citizen; if you break local laws, your U.S. passport won’t help you avoid arrest or prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may be taken in for questioning if you don’t have your passport; certain actions that are legal at home may be illegal in Australia (e.g., photographing certain buildings). Request embassy/consulate notification if detained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Severe penalties for drug offenses and sexual crimes
rubrics_metrics.description: Penalties for possessing, using, or trafficking illegal drugs in Australia are severe, and convicted offenders can expect long jail sentences and heavy fines; engaging in sexual conduct with children or using/disseminating child pornography is prosecutable in the U.S. and abroad.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that objectionable material (child pornography, bestiality, explicit sexual violence, etc.) is subject to declaration/inspection and may be illegal to bring or possess.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medical care and travel insurance recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: Excellent medical care is available in Australia; serious medical problems requiring hospitalization and/or medical evacuation to the United States can cost tens of thousands of dollars.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most doctors and hospitals expect immediate cash/credit card payments for health services — travel insurance is recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terrorism alert system and vigilance
rubrics_metrics.description: Australia has an alert system for possible terrorist attacks; threat levels range from “low” to “high.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depending on the alert, maintain a high level of vigilance and take appropriate steps to increase security awareness; contact the Australian National Security Hotline for information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Driving rules and road safety (left-side driving)
rubrics_metrics.description: Traffic operates on the left side of the road, and all vehicles use right-hand drive; use caution when crossing streets and when driving.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seat belts are mandatory and fines apply for not wearing them; speed limits are measured in kilometers and enforced with speed cameras; driving while intoxicated is rigorously enforced and random breath testing is common.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rural driving hazards and road train caution
rubrics_metrics.description: Outside major metropolitan areas, many highways are two-lane with long distances between destinations; free-roaming animals (e.g., kangaroos) and 'road-trains' present hazards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Passing road trains is dangerous — pull over to allow oncoming road trains to pass; be cautious on loose gravel shoulders and when driving at high speeds; inexperienced 4WD drivers should exercise care in the outback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mobile phone use while driving
rubrics_metrics.description: Texting or holding your phone while driving is against the law, but you can use a hands-free system to communicate while driving.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comply with local hands-free regulations to avoid fines and improve safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Driver’s license and permit variations by state
rubrics_metrics.description: Each state/territory has different rules about using a foreign driver’s license and the conditions under which a visitor might have to get an international driver’s license.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check specific state/territory requirements before driving; in some cases you can apply for an Australian driver’s license from the state where you will remain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental and natural-resource issues to be aware of
rubrics_metrics.description: Australia faces soil erosion, soil salinity, desertification, habitat clearing, limited freshwater resources, and threats to the Great Barrier Reef from shipping and tourism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These environmental issues are relevant for travelers (e.g., reef protection) and for understanding local conservation restrictions and travel advisories.
